what: The heuristic discovers CVRP objects and predicates semantically from task fact names (loc and visited) and numeric variables by their PNE names. In the constructor it precomputes demands, capacity, max-vehicles, a full distance matrix, and distance-sorted nearest-neighbor lists for all nodes. At evaluation time it reads the current location, current load, used vehicles, and unvisited customers. It then greedily builds a complete remaining route plan: from the current location it repeatedly chooses either the cheapest feasible direct visit or a visit-via-depot when another vehicle is available and that option is cheaper. Feasibility respects current load plus demand <= capacity and vehicles + 1 <= max-vehicles. After all customers are served it adds the final return-to-depot distance. Goal states return 0.0.
why: CVRP search states differ mainly in the set of unvisited customers, current location, current load, and number of vehicles used. The chosen design approximates the remaining routing cost with a fast nearest-neighbor CVRP constructive heuristic. Precomputing sorted nearest-neighbor lists keeps each evaluation cheap while still capturing capacity, vehicle limits, route starts via depot, and final return-to-depot. This gives a much more informative state evaluation than simple goal counts or fully relaxed distance heuristics, and should reduce the number of expanded nodes. The design uses semantic fact names and numeric PNE names rather than hardcoded planner IDs or object names, so it generalizes across CVRP instances.
